transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, uh… mostly work stuff finally pushed me to come in. I’m an electrician, so I’m supposed to be doing estimates or filling out code forms, and I just can’t stay on one thing anymore.

Like, I’ll start an estimate, then a tool noise in the shop catches me, or my phone buzzes, or I suddenly get this idea about how I should reorganize the workshop, and then I’m off doing that. Then I come back and I’ve mixed up which job was which, or I’m halfway into the wrong form. It’s been getting frustrating, and honestly kind of embarrassing.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?

Yeah, definitely. Sitting still feels like I’m just… wasting time, you know? I’ll be at one job site and then I’m thinking about the bid I need to run across town, and then I’ll get back to the workshop and start rewiring a test panel or messing with some home-automation idea I had, even though I haven’t finished the last one.

It’s like I’m going nonstop—job sites, bids, the shop—and if I sit down too long I feel like I should be doing something else.
Do you have trouble following through on instructions or finishing tasks because you lose focus?

Yeah, that’s pretty much the thing that made me come in. I’ll get instructions for an estimate or I’ll be working through a code form, and I’ll mean to finish it, but then some tool clanks in the shop, or my phone lights up, or I’ll suddenly think, “Oh, I should rearrange that whole bench setup,” and then I’m gone doing that.

And then when I come back, I’ve lost where I was, or I’ve mixed one job up with another. Like yesterday I had two forms open and somehow started putting details from the wrong job into one of them. It’s frustrating because I know how to do the work, I just can’t seem to stay on the track long enough to finish it cleanly.
Did you have trouble paying attention or sitting still when you were a kid?

I don’t really know, honestly. I mean, I wasn’t the kid who—well, I don’t remember teachers making a big thing out of it. My mom might remember better than me.

I did have a hard time with some classes, but then again I was always more interested in hands-on stuff. Like shop class, wiring little projects, taking apart radios—those I could do for hours. Regular school stuff kind of blurred together. But I can’t say for sure if I was “restless” as a kid the way you mean.
Did you have more energy or activity level as a child compared to your peers?

I’m not really sure. I don’t have a clear picture of whether I was more energetic than other kids. I mean, I was always into taking stuff apart and running around outside like any kid, but comparing myself to peers back then is hard.

My brother used to climb trees and jump bikes and all that too, so it didn’t seem unusual to me. I’d have to ask my mom, honestly—she’d probably remember if I was bouncing off the walls more than everyone else.
Do you think your difficulty with staying focused and being easily distracted is something that you've experienced your whole life?

No, I don’t think it’s been my whole life, not like this. I mean, I’ve always had little quirks with attention, I guess, like anyone, especially if something’s boring, but this has really been building over maybe the last seven months.

That’s around when we took on the mortgage for the workshop and the equipment, and there’s just been a lot more riding on everything. I keep thinking about the numbers and the space and whether we put the compressor in the wrong corner—sorry, that’s not what you asked. But yeah, the focus problems have been more of a recent thing, like since then.
Did you have any problems with paying attention or completing tasks in school when you were a kid?

I’m not totally sure, to be honest. I don’t remember it being some big ongoing problem where teachers were calling home or anything like that. School was just… school, you know? Some stuff I’d get through, some stuff I’d put off if it was boring.

I was better when it was practical—like if I could actually use my hands or see how something worked. Sitting with worksheets, that kind of thing, I probably wasn’t great at it, but I don’t know if that was attention or just me not caring about the subject. My mom would probably have a clearer answer than I do.
Did your parents or teachers ever express concern about your ability to focus or stay on task when you were a child?

I don’t really remember anyone making a big deal about it. Like, I can’t think of a teacher sitting my parents down and saying, “He can’t focus,” or anything.

I mean, my dad used to tell me to finish what I started, but that could’ve been about anything—cleaning the garage, helping with tools, whatever. He had this whole system for organizing screws and bolts that drove me nuts… but no, I don’t know that it was a concern from school or anything. My mom would probably remember better than I do.
Do you think you had any of these focus or restlessness issues when you were a teenager?

As a teenager? I mean… I don’t really think it was like this back then. I probably had normal teenage stuff, getting bored in class or wanting to be somewhere else, but this level of it feels more recent.

It’s really been building over the last seven months or so, since we took on the mortgage for the workshop and the equipment. That kind of changed everything, you know? Suddenly I’m thinking about payments and tools and whether we set things up right, and then I get pulled off track. But no, I wouldn’t say I remember it being a big teenage thing.
Did you have any problems with paying attention or staying focused during childhood activities, like playing games or working on puzzles?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t really remember puzzles being a big thing for me as a kid. Games, yeah, I played, but I couldn’t tell you if I was losing focus more than other kids or just doing kid stuff.

I remember more the garage and messing around with tools than sitting down with puzzles. Like if something had pieces or I could build it, I’d probably stick with it longer—but that might’ve just been because I liked it. I don’t remember anyone saying I couldn’t stay with things back then.
Did you experience any of these attention or focus problems before the age of 12?

Before 12? I really don’t know. I don’t have a clear memory of that being a thing.

I mean, I remember being a kid and running around, doing kid stuff, and my dad always had me around the garage—he’d be like, “Hold this,” or “Don’t lose that screw,” and then he’d get annoyed if I wasn’t paying attention, but that’s just… dads, right? I don’t remember school calling it out or anyone saying I had a focus problem before that age.

So I guess my answer is I’m not sure, but I don’t remember it being a problem back then.
Did you exhibit any symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity before the age of 12 that your parents or other adults noticed?

I don’t really know, honestly. I don’t remember my parents or teachers making a big thing out of me being inattentive or hyper or anything before I was 12.

I mean, my dad would get on me sometimes if I wasn’t listening in the garage, but he got on everyone about everything—like if a wrench wasn’t where he wanted it, that became a whole speech. So I don’t know if that counts or if that was just normal kid stuff.

No adult ever sat me down like, “You’ve got a problem paying attention,” at least not that I remember.
Did your parents ever mention that you had trouble paying attention or sitting still when you were little?

Not that I remember, no. My parents didn’t really talk like that—like, they weren’t sitting around analyzing whether I could sit still.

My mom might’ve said I was “all over the place” sometimes, but I don’t know if she meant me specifically or just, you know, kids in general. And my dad, if I was fidgeting or not listening, he’d just tell me to knock it off and hold the flashlight steady or whatever. That was kind of his whole thing.

So… I don’t think they ever really mentioned it as a problem. At least not in a way that stuck with me.
Did your parents ever take you to see a doctor because you had trouble paying attention or behaving in school?

I don’t think so. I mean, not that I know of.

I remember going to the doctor for normal kid stuff, like shots or if I got sick, and one time I cut my hand pretty good messing around near my dad’s tools—well, I don’t know if that was before 12 or after—but I don’t remember ever being taken because of school behavior or paying attention.

If the school said something, I wasn’t really part of that conversation, but nobody ever told me, “We had to take you in because you couldn’t behave.” So… I’d say no, or at least I don’t remember that happening.
Do you remember having any problems with paying attention or sitting still when you were in elementary school?

Honestly, I don’t really remember it clearly. Elementary school feels kind of blurry now.

I remember normal stuff, like wanting recess to come faster, staring out the window sometimes, getting bored if the teacher went on too long—but I don’t know if that was a “problem” or just being a kid. And sitting still… I mean, those little desks were uncomfortable, you know? I’d probably mess with my pencil or whatever.

But I don’t remember teachers constantly calling me out for it or anything like that. Nothing that stands out as, like, “yeah, this was a big issue.”
Do you remember your parents or anyone else commenting on your behavior or attention span when you were really little, like before you were 7 years old?

Before 7? I really don’t know. I mean, I don’t have many clear memories from that age.

My mom tells stories sometimes, but it’s more like family stuff—me running around at a barbecue or getting into something I shouldn’t—nothing where she was like, “You couldn’t focus” or “you had behavior issues.” And honestly, before 7, I was probably more focused on cartoons and dinosaurs or whatever I was into then. I had this whole phase with toy trucks, actually—my dad had a real work truck, and I used to think that was the coolest thing.

But, yeah… as far as anyone specifically commenting on my attention span or behavior at that age, I don’t remember hearing that.
Do you recall your parents or other family members mentioning that you had trouble sitting still or paying attention when you were really young, like before you started school?

Before school? I don’t really know. I don’t remember anyone saying that specifically.

My family tells little stories, like me being into random stuff or running around the house, but that seems like normal little-kid stuff. My cousin was apparently way worse about climbing on furniture—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

But no, I can’t recall my parents saying I had trouble sitting still or paying attention before school. If they thought that, they never really told me.
Do you remember your parents or anyone else commenting on you being overly active or having trouble paying attention before you were 7 years old?

Yeah, I know you’re asking basically the same thing, and… no, I don’t really remember anyone saying that about me before I was 7.

Like, my parents might say I was energetic, but that could mean anything. My little nephew now is constantly moving, and everyone just laughs it off, so it’s hard for me to know what counts. Back then nobody sat me down and said, “You had trouble paying attention,” or anything like that.

So… I’m not sure. I don’t have a clear memory of anyone commenting on that.
Did your parents mention that you had symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity before you were 5 years old?

Before 5? I honestly wouldn’t know. My parents haven’t mentioned anything that specific to me, like “you were inattentive” or “hyperactive” at that age.

They mostly talk about funny toddler stories, like me making a mess or being obsessed with some toy, which I guess every little kid does. My mom has this story about me refusing to wear a certain pair of shoes for like a week—actually, I don’t know why I remember that one, she brings it up at holidays.

But no, not that I can recall. Nobody’s ever really told me I had those kinds of symptoms before I was 5.
Are you still experiencing symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity today?

Yeah… today, definitely. That’s actually kind of what finally got me in here.

I’m an electrician, so I’m supposed to be able to sit down and focus on an estimate or a code form, and lately I just… can’t keep it locked in. Like I’ll be halfway through something and a tool noise goes off, or I get a text, or I suddenly think of some idea for my workshop setup, and then I’m off on that.

And then I come back and I’m like, wait, which job was this for? Did I already enter that? It starts getting mixed up. I used to be better at keeping all that straight.

I’m an electrician, so I’m supposed to be able to sit down and focus on an estimate or a code form, and lately I just… can’t keep it locked in. Like I’ll be halfway through something and a tool noise goes off, or I get a text, or I suddenly think of some idea for my workshop setup, and then I’m off on that.

And then I come back and I’m like, wait, which job was this for? Did I already enter that? It starts getting mixed up. I used to be better at keeping all that straight.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty staying focused and being easily distracted, along with symptoms of hyperactivity, like feeling restless and fidgety, have been present for approximately seven months. While the patient does not recall having significant attention or hyperactivity issues as a child, the current symptoms are causing significant distress and impairment in social and occupational functioning.
